title: 1.1 Functions and Function Notation
objectives: Determine whether a relation represents a function.
Find the value of a function.
Determine whether a function is one-to-one.
Use the vertical line test to identify functions.
Graph the functions listed in the library of functions.
headings: Determining Whether a Relation Represents a Function
Finding Input and Output Values of a Function
Determining Whether a Function is One-to-One

items.title: Example 1
items.prompt_text: Determining If Menu Price Lists Are Functions The coffee shop menu, shown in Figure 2 consists of items and their prices. ⓐ Is price a function of the item? ⓑ Is the item a function of the price? Figure 2

items.title: Example 3
items.prompt_text: Using Function Notation for Days in a Month Use function notation to represent a function whose input is the name of a month and output is the number of days in that month. Assume that the domain does not include leap years.

items.title: Example 4
items.prompt_text: Interpreting Function Notation A function $N = f (y)$ gives the number of police officers, $N ,$ in a town in year $y .$ What does $f (2005) = 300$ represent?

items.title: Try It #2

items.title: Example 6
items.prompt_text: Evaluating Functions at Specific Values Evaluate $f (x) = x^{2} + 3 x - 4$ at: ⓐ $2$ ⓑ $a$ ⓒ $a + h$ ⓓ Now evaluate $\frac{f (a + h) - f (a)}{h}$

items.title: Example 7
items.prompt_text: Evaluating Functions Given the function $h (p) = p^{2} + 2 p ,$ evaluate $h (4) .$

items.title: Example 8
items.prompt_text: Solving Functions Given the function $h (p) = p^{2} + 2 p ,$ solve for $h (p) = 3.$

items.title: Example 9
items.prompt_text: Finding the Algebraic Form of a Function Express the relationship $2 n + 6 p = 12$ as a function $p = f (n) ,$ if possible.

items.title: Example 10
items.prompt_text: Expressing the Equation of a Circle as a Function Does the equation $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$ represent a function with $x$ as input and $y$ as output? If so, express the relationship as a function $y = f (x) .$
